correctness.rationale: Properness forces any color used on both shores to appear precisely once at the two endpoints of one deleted matched edge; hence s shared colors correspond to s distinct deleted pairs. Given those, all remaining colors are shore-private set-partition blocks, yielding named-palette falling factorial (q)_{s+k+l}. With s>=2 a shared singleton always survives any one deletion; with s=1 the paired vertex needs an additional private singleton. With s=0 each opposite neighborhood needs either >=2 singleton blocks, one unmatched singleton, or (when all opposite vertices matched) each distinguished vertex occupying a doubleton block. Counting doubleton pairings yields stated Z(p,t,k) and three W_s cases. This proves the full two-variable formula for all m,n>=2,t and integer palettes. Independently brute-enumerated 128 parameter/palette combinations m,n=2..4 and q=1..4 and matched the Stirling-partition formula, including C_4,4,4(4,u)=216+144u^2+24u^4. The four-color constructive bound and s=0..3 casework give precisely the claimed 2/3/4 chromatic exceptions.

originality.rationale: An earlier Resultary 2026 crown-graph theorem already establishes chi_pcf(Cr_n)=2,3,4 and the shared-color-pair lemma; this numerical specialization is NOT new. Its entire RESULT.md explicitly leaves classification of all optimal four-colorings untreated. The assessed contribution instead counts every named-palette coloring, all partial matching deletions and unbalanced shores, and refines shared colors by s. Resultary odd-coloring uses different neighborhood parity; complete multipartite coloring has no deleted matching and cannot imply this polynomial. General conflict-free graph-coloring literature provides the concept and complexity bounds, not the enumerator in inspected material.
residual_risks: The chromatic-number crown specialization and singleton-pair lemma are previously published and must never be claimed new.
An unindexed graph coloring enumerator may contain the polynomial or a stronger general deletion formula.
Proper open-neighborhood condition and deletions forming a matching are essential.
